shortName: Medical College of Georgia at Augusta University

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: Prematriculation is a summer program for incoming medical students who have been accepted to the Medical College of Georgia. This program is by invitation only, and for additional information, students may visit our website at https://www.augusta.edu/mcg/students/.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: For purposes of this policy, any termination of a student's enrollment other than graduation will be considered a withdrawal from the institution. This includes Leave of Absence with the intent to return. The Associate Dean for Student & Multicultural Affairs holds the authority to withdraw a student for disciplinary, academic, or other appropriate reasons. Any withdrawal initiated by the dean or his/her designee shall be considered an administrative withdrawal. Student initiated withdrawals (Leave of Absence) occur for a variety of reasons, including illness, time to better prepare for taking licensing exams, or to spend time in another educational opportunity. Leave of Absence is granted for no more than one calendar year. Stipulations relating to the reason for the time away are stated and agreed upon. The student must maintain regular contact with the Associate Dean for Student & Multicultural Affairs and must provide information supporting the proper use of time in leave of absenc
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: The Medical College of Georgia has a robust listing of student organizations, societies, extracurricular and community-based activities to meet the specific interests of our student population. Activities include, but are not limited to, intramural sports, student-led community clinics, and volunteer opportunities with service-based organizations within the surrounding community.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: MCG's main campus is in Augusta, GA, which is located on the south bank of the Savannah River. Augusta is midway between the Great Smokey Mountains and the Atlantic Ocean.  The thriving city is a leading health care hub with eight area hospitals, including two large Department of Veteran's Affairs facilities and a state psychiatric hospital. A second four-year campus, in partnership with Georgia Southern University, is located in Savannah, GA. Savannah is a charming city on the coast of Georgia, with world-renowned art, architecture, and some of the region's best restaurants.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: On-campus and off-campus housing options are available on either four-year campus.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The Medical College of Georgia provides several targeted support systems for gender and sexual minority students, ranging from student-led clinical opportunities to specialized advocacy organizations.  One of the most prominent support structures is the Equality Clinic of Augusta, which serves as both a healthcare resource and a primary training ground for students.  Additionally, students can connect with peers through the MCG Pride Chapter and the Augusta University Lambda Alliance as well as seek individual support through the MCG Student Affairs Office.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The Medical College of Georgia (MCG) is committed to supporting applicants and learners with disabilities in partnership with Augusta University’s Testing and Disability Services (TDS), which evaluates and approves accommodations in accordance with federal and institutional guidelines. MCG implements approved accommodations across pre-clerkship and clinical settings. A dedicated Learning Specialist provides individualized academic support, including learning assessments, study strategies, time management, test-taking skills, and ongoing coaching. For students with suspected or undocumented learning differences, MCG facilitates referrals for psychoeducational or neuropsychological evaluations to ensure timely access to appropriate accommodations. These coordinated resources reflect MCG’s commitment to fostering an inclusive environment that promotes academic success and professional development.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: For more information, please visit the Office of Learner Well-Being webpage at https://www.augusta.edu/mcg/academic-affairs/wellness/index.php.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The Medical College of Georgia works hard to maintain a collaborative and supportive environment for our students.  Faculty and staff are dedicated to helping each student reach their full potential personally, academically, and professionally by building community and offering a strong infrastructure of innovative student services, programs, and resources.  Additionally, faculty have an open-door policy, which allows students the ability to share feedback as well as to seek support at any time.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Professional- Business attire with white coat.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Upon matriculation, students are assigned an Academic Advisor who provides longitudinal academic counseling, 1-2 times per semester. Individual/group tutoring is available to all students.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Patient encounters begin in year one through both simulated and real patient experiences with Standardized Patients, mannequins, and real patients with both face to face and telehealth encounters.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Weekly clinical cases anchor large & small group learning, laboratories (anatomy, simulation, ultrasound), and clinical skills sessions that utilize standardized patient & real patient encounters.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: There are eight required core clerkships and three required selectives. Students also participate in a variety of clinical electives pertinent to their designated specialty.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: Prematriculation is a program for matriculating first year students. Participants will gain exposure to course material, knowledge and skills needed to be successful in medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: All small group and clinical activities have required attendance. Some lectures do not have required attendance. They are live streamed and recorded.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The Medical College of Georgia is home to the innovative 3+ curriculum, designed to integrate foundational knowledge with hands-on clinical experience, ensuring students are prepared to excel in a rapidly evolving healthcare landscape. With a strong emphasis on innovation, research, and patient-centered care, our program equips students with the skills to make a meaningful impact in medicine.

At MCG, students engage in early clinical experiences within the first weeks of medical school and develop self-directed learning through a dynamic mix of small and large group activities. The 3+ curriculum is structured into three phases:

1. Preclerkship (18 months) –Six modules to build a strong foundation in medical sciences, plus career exploration
2. Clerkship (18 months) – Hands-on patient care experiences in eight core clerkships
3. Enrichment (final year) – Personalized learning through one of four pathways: advanced residency preparation, research concentration, dual degrees, or the 3+ Primary Care Pathway

The 3+ Primary Care Pathway allows select students to complete medical school in three years and directly enter an MCG-affiliated primary care residency program, accelerating their journey to practice.

Throughout their training, students have access to cutting-edge technology, including point-of-care ultrasound and simulation, which are seamlessly integrated across all four years to ensure graduates are practice-ready. Learn more: https://www.augusta.edu/mcg/coffice/
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: As the state’s only public academic medical center, statewide growth of medical education is a priority at the Medical College of Georgia. The continuous expansion of partnerships with physicians and hospitals throughout Georgia ensures that students experience the full spectrum of medicine, from urban tertiary care hospitals to small-town primary care practices. The PGY-1 Pathways is an accelerated program in which students graduate in three years and enter into one of seven primary care residency programs. Students in this program receive tuition remission for years two and three of medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: MCG incorporates a scholarly project into the pre-clerkship curriculum. Students receive close mentorship with faculty who are nationally and internationally distinguished scientists, clinicians, and academic scholars. There are many opportunities available, including basic and biomedical laboratory research, clinical and translational research, community/global health research, and medical education research. Students typically engage a research project at MCG, although additional projects at outside institutions are available. Held each academic year, the Medical College of Georgia’s Medical Scholars Research Day offers the opportunity for students to present their research/scholarship findings to fellow students, faculty, and colleagues. For more information: https://www.augusta.edu/mcg/academic-affairs/faculty-development-and-educational-research/eii/for-students.php.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Students must complete 10 hours per semester of service learning.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Research is integrated into the 3+ curriculum and requires all students to complete a scholarly project. Additional research opportunities are available throughout all four years.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Core clerkships take place at Wellstar MCG Health, the Children's Hospital of Georgia, and various affiliated hospitals and community-based teaching sites throughout the state.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Pass/fail is used for the Foundations of Clinical Practice phase (1-18 months).

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
Founded in 1828, the Medical College of Georgia (MCG) is the state’s flagship public medical school, dedicated to training exceptional physicians and physician-scientists. As Georgia’s only public medical school with an academic medical center, Wellstar MCG Health, we offer students a unique advantage with 23 clinical and six basic science departments, 51 ACGME-accredited residency programs, and eight research centers.

Our statewide campus network provides a wide variety of training opportunities, with two four-year campuses in Augusta and Savannah and regional clinical campus hubs in Albany, Rome, and Wellstar Kennestone in Atlanta. MCG prioritizes Georgia residents and those committed to practicing in the state. Our innovative curriculum ensures students are practice-ready, offering pathways in primary care, advanced residency preparation, dual degrees, and research.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The mission of the Medical College of Georgia (MCG) at Augusta University is to lead the primary & specialty healthcare needs of Georgia & beyond, with an emphasis on caring for underserved communities, by delivering excellence in individualized medical education, transformative research, innovative patient care & community engagement.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout:
In their first three years, students pursue the BS in Cell & Molecular Biology through the Department of Biological Sciences in the College of Science and Mathematics. Then, they begin a four-year program in medicine through either the Medical College of Georgia (MCG).*

Students accepted into these programs will take classes together as a cohort and participate in special opportunities for volunteering, clinical exposure, research, and more.  They will experience a very robust curriculum that exceeds the basic preparatory requirements of the MD, and as a result, they will be well prepared to excel at the next level. 

*Courses taken in the first year of the student’s respective program will be used to satisfy any remaining course requirements needed to complete the BS degree.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Early Decision - 1 Week; Regular Decision - 2 Weeks
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Each letter of recommendation must contain a handwritten signature or appear on official letterhead.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: All applicants are required to submit at least three letters of recommendation through AMCAS. The Admissions Committee will not review an applicant's file without having received at least three letters of recommendation. These can include letters from a Pre-Health Advisory committee (if applicable) and/or personal references. It is strongly recommended that letters be current and relevant with one of the personal recommendations coming from a physician who can speak toward the student's clinical exposure/experience.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Each year, the Medical College of Georgia invites approximately 650 students to interview for admission into the matriculating class of 304 students. Students invited to interview will participate in a Multiple Mini-Interview (MMI) process, which allows for a consistent evaluation of all candidates. Interviews are by invitation only and are virtual. On interview day, students have the opportunity to interact with current students from both four-year campuses.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: Beginning in August of each application cycle.
medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: Interviews are generally held on Tuesdays and Thursdays from August through January.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: All applicants receive a secondary application.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: Applicants must be a GA resident and have a minimum GPA of 3.65 and an MCAT of 509 to apply. The MCAT must be taken no later than June 27, 2026. The primary application deadline is August 1, 2026.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Preference is given to Georgia residents. A maximum of 5% of the incoming class will come from out-of-state applicants.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Out-of-State students represent approximately 5%  (maximum) of the incoming class.
medSchoolApplication.transferContact: Kelli M. Braun, MD, FACOG - Senior Associate Dean for Admissions, Medical College of Georgia
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
MCAT

The MCAT exam is required for admission. The MCAT must not be more than three years old from the date of matriculation, meaning it must not have been taken earlier than January 2024. The last accepted date is September 12, 2026. Updated MCAT deadlines are published on the MCG Admissions webpage: www.augusta.edu/mcg/admissions. 

2026-2027 MCG Acceptance & Withdrawal Procedures 

1.	From February 19, 2027– April 29, 2027, accepted applicants may select the “Plan to Enroll” option in AMCAS via the Choose Your Medical School Tool. Accepted applicants should also submit their signed MCG acceptance agreement within the stated deadlines. 

2.	From April 15, 2027 – April 29, 2027, accepted applicants with multiple admission offers should narrow their choices to three medical schools, with no limit on the number of alternate list offers they may hold.

3.	From April 30, 2027 – June 28, 2027, accepted applicants may select the “Commit to Enroll” option in AMCAS via the Choose Your Medical School Tool. This signals that an applicant is committing to MCG and withdrawing applications 5rom other medical schools. Selecting “Commit to Enroll” does not automatically withdraw acceptances from other medical schools.

4.	Beginning April 30, 2027, if MCG receives notification from AMCAS that an applicant has committed to enroll at another institution, we will withdraw that applicant from the 2027 matriculating class.

5.	Before June 1, 2027 students accepted from the alternate list will have five business days to affirm their acceptance to MCG and withdraw their acceptance from other medical schools. 

6.	Students accepted from the alternate list after June 1, 2027 must affirm their acceptance within 48 hours.

7.	All accepted students are required to "Commit to Enroll" by June 28, 2027. Those participating in the pre-matriculation program must commit by May 15, 2027. If not, MCG may withdraw you from the 2027 matriculating class.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: The MCG Admissions Committee conducts a mission-aligned review of all qualified applicants. The Committee considers a wide range of MCAT scores and takes into account the applicant's metrics in context of their own experiences and attributes. The admissions committee considers all MCAT test scores within three years before the date of matriculation.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: Given the highly competitive nature of the applicant pool, applicants with an MCAT score of less than 496, are typically not considered competitive for interview.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: Given the highly competitive nature of the applicant pool, applicants with GPAs less than 3.0, are typically not considered competitive for interview.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: The MCG Admissions Committee considers all completed relevant coursework in the context of the applicant's completed file.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: The MCG Admissions Committee considers applicants who would have completed a minimum of a bachelor's degree in relevant coursework prior to matriculation.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Please review all pre-requisite coursework information on the MCG website: https://www.augusta.edu/mcg/admissions/application-procedures.php.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo:

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc: The Georgia PGY-1 Pathway is an accelerated, career-focused option within the MCG 3+ curriculum designed to support students with a clear commitment to primary care and service in Georgia, particularly in rural and underserved communities. Through this pathway, students complete all MD degree requirements in three uninterrupted years of core curriculum and then transition directly into the first year of an affiliated primary care residency program (PGY-1).
medSchoolMdPathway.eligibleApplicants: Scholarship-Supported Option (Peach State Scholars) - This option is supported through the Peach State Scholars scholarship program and is available to students pursuing residency training in one of the following primary care specialties: Emergency Medicine, Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Pediatrics, Psychiatry, and General Surgery.
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationProcess: Students apply to the Georgia PGY-1 Pathway after matriculation and participate in extensive advising during the MCG Core curriculum to ensure readiness, alignment with career goals, and successful progression.
medSchoolMdPathway.programRestReq: Students who receive the scholarship commit to two years of practice in underserved areas of Georgia following the successful completion of residency training.
medSchoolMdPathway.residencyAffiliationPathway: Directed residency option available to Three-Year MD students

medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: No time restrictions on prerequisite coursework. Please see augusta.edu/mcg/admissions for more information on prerequisite courses.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The Admissions Committee conducts a comprehensive review of qualified applicants, seeking individuals reflective of our state, with preference given to Georgia residents, those aligned with MCG's mission and those demonstrating a desire to practice medicine in Georgia. Additional characteristics evaluated by the committee can be found on the admissions website: www.augusta.edu/mcg/admissions.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Clinical exposure in a healthcare environment is required. Clinical experience can be voluntary or paid and may include (but is not limited to) volunteering in a healthcare setting, experience as an EMT, MA, CNA, PCT, etc. Direct shadowing is not required.
